newsitem.title: USA: New Year's seen as marker for stock trend.
newsitem.headline: New Year's seen as marker for stock trend.

text.p: Wall Street will suffer from a split personality next week as the New Year provides a demarcation line for sentiment in the stock market.
Analysts expect equities to continue last week's rally in the early part of the week, then suffer a decline as investors begin to worry whether the economy will overheat.

"This week looks like it might a little bit more exciting," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "We're going to start to see what the economy did in December, and the pace in bonds and stocks could quicken quite a bit."
The Dow Jones industrial average rose for the second week in a row this week, confirming the Santa Clause theory that stocks rally nearly every year during Christmas.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 14.23 points to a record 6,560.91 on Friday, topping the previous record of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25. For the week, the Dow rose 76.51 points.
"The first part of the week will be a continuation of (this) week, not up big, but more money will be drifting into the market," said Alfred Kugel, investment strategist at Stein Roe.
Portfolio managers will use the last days of the year to add big-capitalisation stock holdings as a way to beef up full-year returns.

"After the first of the year, the incentive for people (to buy) will disappear, and we could see some softness and profit taking," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.

The week will be relatively light on economic data. On Monday, the Conference Board issues data on leading indicators for November, with the forecast at up 0.1 percent, after a 0.1 percent gain in October.
On Thursday, the National Association of Purchasing Management will release the December report, with the index expected at 51.5, down from 52.7 in November.
A reading above 50 suggests economic expansion, while a reading below 50 points to contraction.

"Both will give us a strong sense of what happened in the economy in December," said Johnson. "We have a hint that it weakened ... and the NAPM report could confirm it. They will be watched very carefully."
Analysts said the market has been benefiting from a healthy economy.

"We're still in that Goldilocks economy, growing moderately -- not too strong and not too weak," Kugel said. "There's not any significant likelihood that the Federal Reserve will tighten rates. The economy is positive, and money needs to be invested."
The week is expected to be quiet as New Year's Day falls on Wednesday.

"There will be an absence of research recommendations," said Eric Miller, chief investment officer at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. "There's also the absence of new issues. The supply is a little lighter than it might normally be."

Among other stock indexes, the technology studded Nasdaq Composite index fell 3.19 Friday to 1,291.38. The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 0.97 to 756.79 -- just shy of its record of 757.03 also set on Nov. 25.
